messages:
sara: kicking off py/ts SDK canary publish now. I see deploy-bot flagged a signer mismatch for the Python wheel on the mirror — holding everything.

deploy-bot: publish job #7423 started
deploy-bot: ERROR signing: wheel signature does not match upstream key (expected 0xA1B2C3D4, got 0xDEADBEEF)

omar: ack. pausing the TS canary too? want to avoid half-published state.

sara: yes pause TS. I'm tagging the canary as 'on-hold' in shiproom notes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

liam: quick checklist:
- verify wheel artifacts locally `pip wheel .` + `gpg --verify dist/*.whl.asc`
- check CI signing key used for the build (circleci secret rotation last week?)

release-eng: likely cause = ephemeral signing key rotated yesterday (rotated by ops). If the CI still cached old key ID that could flip signatures.

sara: logs show CI used key id 0xDEADBEEF for the failing wheels. ops rotated to A1B2C3D4 as of 2026-03-19 03:22 UTC.

omar: recommended short-term mitigation: republish the *previous* canary as a pinned fallback so consumers on the canary cohort don't break. We can set dist-tags and unpublish the broken wheel.

liam: commands for fallback: (run on release host)
```
# npm side (TS client)
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk-js@1.3.2 canary-fallback
npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk-js canary   # remove broken tag
# python side (pip index)
# if wheel corrupted, add a new 'canary-fallback' release and point docs/CI at it
```

release-eng: for python we should avoid unpublishing if pypi already mirrored. Instead: republish correct-signed wheel with a +rev suffix (1.3.3+fixsig) and then update the canary pointer. That avoids pypi yanking issues.

sara: agreed. republish path: build with CI using ops-confirmed key, tag +rev, promote to canary after smoke.

omar: action items:
- sara: coordinate republish (py +ts) and confirm CI key in use
- liam: run local verification script + checksum audit `scripts/checksum-audit.sh`
- release-eng: draft a small release note entry explaining the hold + republish and deprecation note for legacy sync client if consumers ask

liam: when republishing, include this quick smoke test (run in a fresh venv):
```
python -m venv /tmp/sdk-smoke && source /tmp/sdk-smoke/bin/activate
pip install --index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple redwood-sdk==1.3.3+fixsig
python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__version__)"
```

sara: I'll also push a shiproom comment with the canary cohort paused and a link to the failing CI job: https://ci.redwood.example/7423

deploy-bot: publish job #7423 status = FAILED (signer-mismatch)

release-eng: wording for the release note (short):
"Canary publish paused due to artifact signing mismatch. A corrected republish (1.3.3+fixsig) will be issued and promoted to canary once CI keys are validated. No user-facing changes expected; if you are on canary please pin to stable 1.3.2 until republish completes."

sara: ok we will use that. tagging @support to watch for tickets.

omar: estimate: republish + verification ~ 30–45m if ops confirms key. If ops needs new key provisioning add +2h.

liam: small extra: add an audit entry to the release checklist about key rotation timestamp so future CI runs check key ID before signing. I can PR a check.

sara: perfect. assigning: sara (republish coordination), liam (verification/audit PR), omar (canary fallback tag ops), release-eng (release note). I'll update shiproom at each milestone.

deploy-bot: waiting for manual trigger to rerun publish once CI creds validated.

sara: manual trigger scheduled after ops confirms key. Will post back here when republish completes. :white_check_mark:
